name: Cardiovascular embryology
can: Describe embryological development of the cardiovascular system, including valves, chambers, and blood vessels.

name: Heart and vessel histology
can: Describe microscopic anatomy of the heart and blood vessels.

name: Heart, great vessels, and pericardium
can: Describe location, structure, and boundaries of the heart, major vessels, and pericardium.

name: Heart valves and the cardiac cycle
can: Describe location and explain heart valve function in relation to the cardiac cycle.

name: Cardiac muscle contraction
can: Explain physiological basis of contraction in cardiac muscle.

name: Cardiac cycle and its regulation
can: Explain functions and regulatory mechanisms of the cardiac cycle.

name: Conduction system and the ECG
can: Describe location, function, autonomic regulation, and electrical measurement of the conduction system.

name: Coronary circulation
can: Describe location and branching patterns of coronary arteries and circulatory pathways of blood supply.

name: Blood distribution to body regions
can: Describe anatomical patterns of blood distribution to somatic and visceral areas.

name: Lymphatic vessels, tissues, and organs
can: Describe location, structure, circulatory pathways, and functions of lymphatic vessels, tissues, and organs.

name: Hemodynamics and blood flow regulation
can: Describe forces involved in circulation of blood and lymph, and regulation of blood flow.

name: Exercise and the cardiovascular system
can: Explain acute and adaptive effects of exercise on the cardiovascular system.

name: Cardiovascular biochemistry and nutrition
can: Explain biochemistry of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, vitamins, minerals, and co-factors as they relate to cardiovascular function and pathology.

name: Cardiovascular genetics
can: Describe features and explain principles of gene expression, control, cell cycle regulation, and consequences of genetic abnormalities underlying cardiovascular disease.

name: Heart and lung interactions
can: Explain relationship between cardiovascular and pulmonary systems.

name: Immune responses in cardiovascular disease
can: Describe activation of innate and adaptive immune mechanisms by microbial pathogens, cancer/tumors, antigens, and vaccines; describe inflammatory, autoimmune, and hypersensitivity immune responses.

name: Cardiovascular pathogens
can: Explain morphology, replication/life cycle, transmission (including vectors), mechanisms of infection, virulence factors, and genetic characteristics of common microbial pathogens causing listed conditions.

name: Hypertensive heart diseases
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of hypertensive heart diseases: Pulmonary hypertension; Systemic hypertension.

name: Congestive heart failure
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of congestive heart failure: Left-sided; Right-sided.

name: Ischemic heart disease
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of ischemic heart disease: Angina pectoris; Chronic ischemic heart disease; Myocardial infarction (MI).

name: Valvular heart diseases
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of valvular heart diseases: Aortic stenosis/insufficiency; Mitral stenosis/insufficiency; Endocarditis; Mitral valve prolapse (MVP); Rheumatic heart disease; Carcinoid heart disease.

name: Primary myocardial diseases
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of primary myocardial diseases: Cardiomyopathies (dilated, restrictive, hypertrophic); Myocarditis.

name: Pericardial disease
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of pericardial disease: Metastatic disease; Pericardial effusions; Pericarditis (primary and secondary).

name: Congenital heart conditions
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of congenital heart conditions: Bicuspid aortic valve; Patent ductus arteriosus; Septal defects (interventricular, atrial); Tetralogy of Fallot.

name: Hemodynamic conditions
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of hemodynamic conditions: Embolism; Hemorrhage; Infarction; Edema; Shock; Thrombosis.

name: Vascular conditions
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of vascular conditions: Aneurysm; Aortic dissection; Arteriosclerosis and atherosclerosis; Familial hypercholesterolemia; Giant cell arteritis (temporal arteritis); Peripheral arterial disease (PAD); Pulmonary embolism (PE); Raynaud phenomenon (primary and secondary); Thromboangiitis obliterans; Thrombosis, deep vein (DVT); Varicose veins; Vasculitis.

name: Vascular neoplasms
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of vascular neoplasms: Hemangiomas; Kaposi sarcoma.

name: Infectious vascular diseases
can: Explain pathogenesis and identify etiology, risk factors, complications, and clinical characteristics of infectious vascular diseases: Bacterial endocarditis; Chagas disease; Lyme disease; Rocky Mountain spotted fever; Viral hemorrhagic fever (yellow fever, Dengue fever, filoviruses); Viral myocarditis.
